title: Preemptive fairness ledger and operator-snooze for tenant-aware load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During multi-region overload events we need a predictable, equitable way to shed load that preserves high-SLO customers while minimizing cross-tenant unfairness and oscillation. Existing token-bucket and lane-based shedders apply blunt admission rules that can starve low-volume but latency-sensitive tenants and lack an operator-friendly temporary override.

Proposal: Implement a preemptive fairness ledger that tracks short-window credit balances per-tenant and per-customer-class, allowing the admission layer to make proportional preemptive drops instead of binary eviction. Add an operator 'snooze' action that temporarily pauses automatic shedding for a tenant (for incident mitigation or customer escalations) with audit log entries and automated decay. Integrate graceful degradation modes: soft-trim (partial-response token trimming), model-fallback (quantized/cheaper variant), and delayed-execute (defer to reservoir with callback). The ledger will feed the admission controller and be considered alongside SLO tiers, regional headroom, and model capacity signals.

Why different: This approach is explicitly credit-based and preemptive (anticipatory smoothing) rather than purely reactive queue eviction. The operator-snooze is an operational affordance to make human-in-the-loop mitigations without permanently breaking fairness, with safety decay to avoid abuse.

Scope: core admission controller changes (runtime), controller API surface for ledger and snooze, Console UI affordance for operators to view/trigger snooze, audit logs, metrics and runbook updates, automated tests and chaos scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger maintained per-tenant with sliding window credit that updates on accepted/denied requests
Admission controller uses ledger balance + SLO tier + region headroom to compute probabilistic preemptive drop rate
Operator snooze API pauses automated shedding for a tenant for a configurable TTL and writes auditable events
Snooze has automated decay (max TTL + cooldown) to prevent indefinite exemptions
Graceful degradation modes (soft-trim, model-fallback, delayed-execute) selectable by policy and triggered when preemptive drop rate > threshold
End-to-end tests simulating regional overload verify no tenant starvation and improved p95 latency for P0 clients compared to baseline
Console shows ledger balances, active snoozes, and suggested escalations; audit log searchable
Runbook updated with steps for operator snooze, rollback, and post-incident fairness reconciliation
implementation_notes: Ledger: in-memory ring with periodic durable checkpoint to metastore; TTL 60s sliding window by default
Credit delta: accepted +1, soft-degrade -0.5, hard-reject -2 (configurable per tier)
Admission decision: compute effective_score = weighted(ledger_balance, sla_score, region_headroom, recent_error_rate); map to drop probability via sigmoid function
Operator snooze: RBAC-protected REST endpoint; supports reason, TTL, and emergency flag; recorded in audit log with user and request id

Graceful modes: soft-trim modifies max_output_tokens header; model-fallback maps to quantized variant registered in model catalog; delayed-execute returns 202 with callback token and queues request into reservoir
Safety: limit concurrent snoozes per-region to avoid exploit; snooze cannot override tenant quotas or security policies
Metrics: ledger_balance_gauge, preemptive_drop_rate, snooze_active_count, soft_trim_rate, fallback_rate, delayed_exec_queue_length
risks_and_tradeoffs: Complexity: ledger adds state; need efficient sharding to avoid added latency on admission path
Fairness tuning: misconfigured weights could create perverse incentives—requires careful defaults and telemetry
Operator misuse: snooze can be abused to bypass shedding; mitigated by RBAC, TTLs, cooldowns and audit visibility
Consistency during failover: ledger checkpoints must be resilient to region failover; on failover we must avoid double-counting credits
Observable cost: additional metrics and storage impact; must budget retention and cardinality
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-experimental; simulate-only mode where preemptive drop suggestions are logged but not applied
2) Canary: enable apply mode for 5% of traffic across low-impact tenants in a single region
3) Evaluate metrics for 48h; adjust weights and thresholds
4) Gradually increase blended traffic to 25% then 100% for region A
5) Expose operator snooze behind Console beta with audit trail; require two-person approval for snoozes > 30m for P0 tenants
6) Cross-region rollout with ledger checkpoint/replication verification and failover drills
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger arithmetic and decay semantics
Admission integration tests comparing baseline token-bucket to ledger preemptive drops under synthetic workloads
Chaos test: region outage and failover ensures ledger checkpoint recovers and no credit duplication
Operator flow e2e test: create snooze, verify admission accepts, TTL expires and audit log entry present
Load test with mixed SLA tenants measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and successful request rate improvements for P1/P0 customers
notes: Related research: implement anticipatory smoothing using short-window EWMA of ingress and queue occupancy
Consult with Product on recommended defaults for credit weights per SLA tier
Follow security review if console exposes bulk-snooze or programmatic snooze via public API
Link proposed Console mockups in PRD: https://confluence.internal.redwood/projects/RRPS/pages/ledger-snooze-mockups
comments: 2026-02-22 Marcus Green: Initial spike complete — in-memory ledger prototype meets latency budget (p50 add ~0.4ms). Need to validate memory overhead at 1M tenants.
2026-03-01 Design review: PMs asked for tenant-level soft-degrade presets per plan (chatbot, embeddings, search). Action: add presets and allow Console overrides.
2026-03-05 Security: suggested RBAC review for snooze endpoint; added requirement for audit events and retention policy.
2026-03-10 Load test: under synthetic mixed workload, preemptive ledger reduced hard rejections by 18% and improved P0 p95 by ~120ms in region-A (see loadboard).

2026-03-14 Marcus Green: Started canary rollout in region-A with feature flag 'ledger-preemptive-apply'; observing drop-rate smoothing but need to tweak sigmoid steepness. Next: refine weights and add Console visibility for active balances.
